paragraphs: On Saturday, there was a school sale in the school hall. It rained all morning, so many people came with umbrellas. Lily and May worked at the Information desk. Mia worked at the table next to them. Her table had bracelets, necklaces, and cups of juice. The Explorers' green flag stood on the desk. A big sign on the desk said, "Information." Under the sign, there was a price list. May wrote the prices in big letters with a black pen.
"Bracelets, ten baht." "Necklaces, twenty baht." "Umbrellas, forty baht." "Mango juice, fifteen baht for a cup." "A small taste of juice is free." Lily read the list to every person with a smile.

A girl asked, "Is a bracelet ten baht?" "Yes, it is," said Lily. A woman asked, "Is a necklace thirty baht?" "No, it is not," said May. "A necklace is twenty baht, so it is cheap." "Can I taste the juice first?" asked an old man. "Yes, you can," said May. "Mia has a small cup for you." The man tasted the juice and smiled. "It is cold and sweet," he said. "Is the red umbrella expensive?" asked a boy. "It is forty baht, so it is the most expensive thing here," said Lily.

The door of the hall had a sign, "PULL." A little girl tried to push it, but it did not open. "Pull the door," said May with a smile. The girl pulled it, and the door opened. She walked in with her mom and said, "Thank you!" "Where are the bracelets?" asked the mom. "They are on Mia's table, next to the juice," said Lily.
At twelve o'clock, the sale finished. Lily put the sign and the price list in a box. "The Information desk was the best job," said May. "Today we helped many people."
